reproducibility.description: Read-only security scan. Inputs: tool/bundler/*.rb.lock + installed gem sources + rubygems.org API. Outputs: /tmp/scan/* intermediates and this report only. No gem source or lockfile is modified; no gem is upgraded.
prerequisites: bundle-audit update                        # clones rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (pinned commit in scanner_components.advisory_db_commit)

Install all 7 bundles FROZEN for source scanning (does not alter locks): for f in dev lint release rubocop standard test vendor; do (cd tool/bundler && BUNDLE_GEMFILE=${f}_gems.rb bundle install --frozen); done
run_sequence: 1. bundle-audit check --no-update on each tool/bundler/*.rb.lock (copied to a temp Gemfile.lock); capture full output incl. EXIT codes -> audit_all.txt
2. build_manifest.rb  -> manifest.json          (enumerate full direct+transitive tree from all 7 lockfiles; flag non-rubygems sources)
3. parse_cve.rb       -> cve_findings.json       (dedup platform/cross-lockfile dupes into distinct gem,version,advisory)
4. scan_deser.rb      -> deser_findings.json     (Marshal.load/restore, YAML.load non-safe, Psych.load w/o permitted_classes across all installed .rb)
6. scan_confusion.rb  -> confusion_findings.json (rubygems.org existence/version checks + typosquat variant probing)
reproducibility.one_command: bash /tmp/scan/run_all.sh   # executes steps 1-7 and prints the measured SCAN_DURATION_SECONDS
reproducibility.determinism_note: Steps 2-5 are deterministic given fixed lockfiles + installed gems (byte-identical across runs). Step 1 (CVE) is pinned to advisory_db_commit. Step 6 queries rubygems.org; the FINDINGS are stable across runs, only volatile public-download counts may vary.

result_rationale.pass_condition: PASS iff cve_findings, deserialization_findings, dependency_confusion_findings, and injection_findings are ALL empty
result_rationale.driver: FAIL is driven primarily by 34 CVE/advisory findings in dependency lockfiles; deserialization/injection arrays are risk-surface inventories (largely trusted-input/by-design, see remediation_summary), and dependency_confusion findings are low-risk (git-pinned, upstream-owned names).

remediation_summary.remediation_mode: report-only (this is the SCAN run; gem upgrades / Gemfile.lock changes require a SEPARATE explicit remediation confirmation step per directive system boundaries)

cve.note: All 34 advisories have an available fixed version. Recommended upgrades target the tool/bundler/*.rb.lock pins (dev/test/lint/release tooling). Not applied here per scan-only boundary; the affected lockfiles are out-of-scope for modification in this task.

deserialization.recommended_action: Risk-surface inventory. For untrusted input: prefer YAML.safe_load / Psych.load(permitted_classes:) over YAML.load/unsafe_load; avoid Marshal.load on untrusted data. ALL flagged executable sites here operate on trusted data (precompiled gem data tables, worker-process IPC, ri caches) or are doc-comments/tests; the one by-design case (rack-session cookie Marshal) depends on cookie signing secret. No code change required in trusted-input contexts.
deserialization.mitigation: If any flagged gem is later fed untrusted serialized input, replace with safe deserialization APIs and validate cookie/session secrets (rack-session).

dependency_confusion.recommended_action: Keep the explicit GIT source+revision pins in vendor_gems.rb.lock. The 2 flagged names (net-http, net-http-persistent) have higher PUBLIC versions but the public names are owned by the same upstreams and Bundler will not substitute them while the git source is pinned. No action required; low risk.
dependency_confusion.mitigation: Optionally vendor these git deps into the repo (the bundler vendoring flow already does this) to remove any resolver ambiguity. No typosquatted dependencies were found (all 103 rubygems names are the dominant legitimate packages).

injection.recommended_action: Risk-surface inventory. 0 SQL-injection surfaces (no ActiveRecord/DB layer). All command/template sites are in C-extension build scripts, dev/test/CLI tooling, and template-engine adapters operating on trusted inputs (ENV, file paths, build configs, developer commands). No external-untrusted-input path exists in this dev/build/test dependency set.
injection.mitigation: If any flagged tooling is repurposed to handle untrusted input, use array-form system()/exec(), Shellwords.escape for interpolated commands, and parameterized queries / autoescaped templates.

out_of_scope_notes.scan_only_boundary: Per directive system boundaries this run does NOT modify gem sources or Gemfile.lock entries and does NOT upgrade gems. Applying the 34 CVE remediations (and any other fix) requires a SEPARATE explicit confirmation step distinct from this scan run.
out_of_scope_notes.report_placement: Deliverable placed at tool/bundler/ (beside the scanned lockfiles), NOT repo root. Rationale: the Rakefile :check_manifest task exercised by test/rubygems/test_project_sanity.rb compares Manifest.txt against `git ls-files` filtered by an exclude regex (\A(?:\.|bundler/(?!lib|exe|[^/]+\.md|bundler.gemspec)|tool/|Rakefile|bin|test|doc)). A committed root-level file is NOT excluded and would break that test; the tool/ prefix IS excluded. Manifest.txt is out-of-scope and intentionally left unmodified, which also keeps this scan artifact out of the packaged rubygems-update gem.

platform_conditional_gems_not_installed.reason: Not installable/needed on x86_64-linux MRI: ffi-win32-extensions/win32-process/wmi-lite are Windows-only; jar-dependencies is JRuby-only; mini_portile2 is a nokogiri build-dep superseded by the precompiled native gem; the ffi mingw variant is Windows. They appear in lockfiles + dependency_manifest (NOT silently skipped) but have no on-disk .rb sources to scan on this platform.
platform_conditional_gems_not_installed.coverage_impact: None: deserialization & injection scans cover 100% of the .rb files that ARE installed on this platform (4902 files).

out_of_scope_notes.git_sourced_gems: vendor_gems.rb pins 4 gems to git revisions (molinillo, net-http, net-http-persistent, pub_grub). Two (net-http, net-http-persistent) have higher public rubygems.org versions -> reported as dependency_confusion findings, but LOW risk: the public names are owned by the same upstreams and Bundler honors the explicit git-source pin. Documented for awareness; no modification performed.
